lowered.reason: The scenario needs a FIFO or device link planted on disk inside the install being read. Git cannot commit a FIFO. open() skips the checkout's instrumenter whenever git tracks anything under node_modules (trackedInstall), so a head can't supply the node_modules through the diff. The other callers read Melian's own install (code-version.ts via import.meta.url, and the 'melian' source). Reaching the bug needs a local actor, or a hostile install script, that already controls the filesystem. That is a narrow robustness gap, not a head-controlled hang.

verification.reason: The probe failed again, and it exercises the head code. It loads the head's installed-packages.ts, stubs only canonicalJson (which Walk.#release doesn't use), and calls Install.read on a module under a node_modules that holds a FIFO at evil/package.json. In #release, existsSync is true for a FIFO. readFileSync then opens it for reading, which blocks forever with no writer. The try/catch only handles thrown errors, so nothing guards this. There is no lstat or isFile check and no size bound, and the same call would follow a symlink to /dev/zero. The timeout comes from that read, not from a probe bug.

Why: A crash must not double the model spend, nor let an older verdict overwrite a newer one

verification.reason: At head, `reusable` is `melianInstall().identified && ...` (review.ts 3386-3387) and is passed to `runLenses`. In `own`, `attach` requires `reusable` (1857-1863), so an unidentified install never attaches to the stored task of the same head and selection. A crash-resume review therefore creates a new LensTask and aborts the replaced one (1906-1921). The earlier lens conversations are not resumed, and the model spend is paid again. Base had no `reusable` gate, so a same-selection index entry always attached. That is the behaviour of the ACTIVE decision "Review attachment", which says a repeat call attaches and never duplicates because a crash must not double model spend. That reason still holds for an unidentified install, which is a legitimate state (`npm link`, PnP). The head decision file explicitly accepts the result ("the second review asks every lens again"), but head text does not excuse the departure. Nothing in the code separates crash-resume of the same process's task from a collision with another install's key, so a same-install crash recovery loses its protection too. The narrow trigger (only unidentified installs) fits P2.

evidence.snippet: A link out of the install, such as `npm link yaml` to `/work/yaml`, names a place the walk cannot read without walking the host. It records the fixed entry `["node_modules/yaml", "links outside"]`, adds the place to `outside`, and walks no further. The digest stays deterministic, and `identified` reads false. No value drawn at random enters any key, so rule 6 of [the identity guideline](../guidelines/identity.md#rules) stands as written, and this decision amends nothing there.

verification.reason: The trace holds in the code. `Install.read` takes the outermost ancestor that holds a `node_modules` as the root (lines 49-50). A stray `/home/u/node_modules` therefore moves the root up to `/home/u`. `#beneath(target)` (134-137) then accepts `/home/u/work/yaml`, so `#follow` records `links` and not `links outside`, and pushes nothing to `outside`. In `package` mode only the target's `package.json` is keyed (175-178). `identified` stays true, so `checkReusable` passes. An edit to `dist/compose.js` leaves the digest unchanged, and a guardrails run decided by the old parser is reused. The `file:./vendor/yaml` link inside the checkout takes the same path with no stray directory at all. The decision, line 79, promises that an `npm link` to a package outside Melian's tree leaves the install unidentified and reuses nothing. Line 32 only excuses unkeyed files for workspace packages, whose source "the code version covers". A forked or vendored dependency isn't covered by Melian's code version, so that justification doesn't hold for it. The widened root also makes the outcome depend on whether an unrelated `~/node_modules` exists. I traced the code but did not run it.

It names which `melian` ran and warns when it lies inside the checkout. The `clone` line names the linked git clone, its commit, and whether its tree is clean. It warns when the clone is dirty or git cannot read it. An install under `node_modules` omits that line. Doctor also checks the state directory and whether it is writable. Its `records` line, when the checkout has an `origin`, fetches the `melian/state` branch's tip into the store's own repository. It names, as a warning, up to five files on it that Melian did not write, which refuse calls until a writer removes them, or warns that the branch cannot be read. Opening the store sweeps what killed calls left in the state directory, and the line warns about what that sweep left: up to five leftovers it kept because it cannot tell their maker is gone, up to five of an exited call it could not remove, how many stale ones it ran out of time to remove, or left because it could not list every leftover, which the next open removes, that it stopped listing at its bound of 1,000 leftovers, and a process table it could not read, which sweeps nothing and keeps every leftover it found. It names them after the branch's own warning when the branch cannot be read, since the sweep ran when the store opened. A sweep that removed all it found says nothing. With it on, the line says the branch's writers are trusted as the repository's writers. With it off, it warns that only the trusted host may write `melian/state`, since doctor cannot check who may push to it. When no policy can be read, it warns that who may write the branch is unknown.
